title: Web: the Vacationing and Google-Calendar status presets send a status_timeout the API rejects, so saving fails silently and the status is stored without an expiry
description:
## Summary

The "Set a status" modal offers six presets. Two of them write a `duration` string straight into the `status_timeout` field sent to `POST /api/v1/profile/change-status`, and the API rejects both values:

- `Vacationing` uses `duration: "Don’t clear"` (line 45). The backend only accepts ASCII `dont-clear` / `don't-clear` / `dont clear` / `don't clear`; this preset uses a typographic apostrophe (U+2019), so after `strings.ToLower` it is still `don’t clear` and falls into the `default` branch.
- `In a meeting` under `Automatically updates` uses `duration: "Based on your Google Calendar"` (line 55), which is not a recognised value at all.

Picking either preset therefore produces `400 Bad Request` with `invalid expiry value: ...`. Because `handleSubmit` only reacts to `200/201` and shows no error, the dialog stays open with no feedback, while the backend has already written the status text/emoji before the parse fails.

## Where - frontend

`src/app/(client)/[org]/_components/status/index.tsx`
- Lines 45 and 55: the two offending preset durations.
- Line 80: `const [removeAfter, setRemoveAfter] = useState("Today")`; the preset click handler assigns `setRemoveAfter(item.duration)`.
- Lines 106-113: `removeOptions` are `"30 minutes"`, `"1 hour"`, `"Today"`, `"This week"`, `"dont-clear"` - the `<select>` can only render those five values, so the invalid preset value is never visible: the select falls back to displaying the first option while the state still holds `Don’t clear`.
- Lines 120-139: `handleSubmit` sends `status_timeout: removeAfter` (line 126) and only closes on `res?.status === 200 || res?.status === 201`; there is no `else` branch, no toast and no error state.

## Where - backend

- `internal/models/profile.go:344-405` - `ParseStatusExpiry` accepts `30 seconds`, `30 minutes`, `1 hour`, `today`, `this week`, `dont-clear`/`don't-clear`/`dont clear`/`don't clear`, and otherwise returns `fmt.Errorf("invalid expiry value: %s", expiryStr)` (line 403).
- `internal/models/profile.go:250-262` - `UpdateProfileStatus` writes `text`, `icon` and the raw `status_timeout` **before** any expiry parsing happens.
- `services/profile/profile.go:445-452` - after that write, `ParseStatusExpiry(statusTimeout)` returns the error and the request is answered with `400`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in on the web app and open the status modal (profile menu -> Set a status).
2. Click the `Vacationing` preset (or `In a meeting` in the `Automatically updates` section). The text field fills with `Vacationing` and the duration state becomes `Don’t clear`.
3. Click the save button.
4. The request body contains `"status_timeout":"Don’t clear"` and the API answers `400` `invalid expiry value: Don’t clear`.
5. The dialog stays open with no message, and the profile already holds the status text with an unparseable `status_timeout`, so no auto-clear job is scheduled.

Expected: the preset saves, with `status_timeout` normalised to a value the API accepts (`dont-clear` for `Vacationing`).

Actual: `400`, silent failure, partially written status.

## Suggested fix

- Use the API value `dont-clear` for the `Vacationing` preset, and give the calendar preset a real duration or its own non-expiring flag.
- Show an error toast when the response is not `200/201`.
- Backend: normalise U+2019 to `'` and collapse whitespace before the `switch`, and validate before writing the profile row.

Source links: https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-fe/blob/877af23/src/app/(client)/%5Borg%5D/_components/status/index.tsx#L45 , https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/internal/models/profile.go#L403 , https://github.com/Zedu-Endor/zedu-be/blob/67db4db20f1876a644f6b305575303aa312c5ce0/services/profile/profile.go#L445
